key_insight: A finite spanwise-oscillating wall reduced turbulent boundary-layer drag by 32%, with exponential skin-friction onset and recovery length scales of 0.6δ and 0.9δ.
engineering_relevance: These response lengths can inform the sizing and placement of finite wall-actuation patches for turbulent drag control.
method: Study spatial boundary-layer response at Reτ = 652, T+ ≈ 101 and A+ ≈ 7.
Estimate skin friction using near-wall arctangent nonlinear regression without resolving the viscous sublayer.
Track turbulence statistics and conditional quadrant events across onset and recovery.
evidence_signal: The regression method was assessed against reference DNS data and reproduced experimental measurement-error trends; most Reynolds-stress responses had fitted length scales within 0.5δ.
watch_item: Net energy savings are not established by the reported drag reduction alone, and the shear-stress peak responds over a substantially longer distance than other stress measures.
paper_title: Spatially developing drag reduction across a finite oscillating wall
